subject.title: Tool-result truncation jitter invalidates prompt-cache prefixes — quantize truncation to stable steps

question: Should core prioritize byte-stable prompt prefixes for compatible-provider caching when doing so may conservatively truncate historical tool results before the exact current-turn budget requires it?
rationale: The issue proposes a global trade-off between retained tool context and cache reuse; source evidence establishes adjacent dynamic recovery behavior but does not determine the acceptable loss budget or bucket policy.

options.title: Validate then stabilize
options.body: Capture current-main prompt/cache telemetry and implement deterministic bucketed truncation only if it preserves overflow safety and useful-context expectations.

options.title: Keep adaptive truncation
options.body: Retain the exact per-turn budget policy and document cache churn as an accepted trade-off for maximum retained tool-result context.

recommendation.title: Validate then stabilize
recommendation.body: Capture current-main prompt/cache telemetry and implement deterministic bucketed truncation only if it preserves overflow safety and useful-context expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on context-budget propagation makes this the closest available ownership signal for the required policy trade-off.
